form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

labs.title: Environment Setup and Configuration Parsing
labs.exercise: Set up the local development environment, configure the AI coding agent framework, and parse configuration files to identify active components.
labs.notes: Focus on understanding the configuration structure before writing code.

labs.title: Implementing Custom Tools and MCP Bindings
labs.exercise: Implement a custom local file-search tool and register it with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to extend agent capabilities.
labs.notes: Requires local testing of MCP tool schemas.

labs.title: Configuring Agent Skills and Bindings
labs.exercise: Configure and bind custom tools to a code-refactoring agent, ensuring the agent can invoke them correctly during local refactoring tasks.
labs.notes: Verify that no configuration warnings are reported.

labs.title: Refining Skills and Specification Templates
labs.exercise: Refine agent skills for complex refactoring tasks and translate a natural language use case into a structured specification template.
labs.notes: Transitioning from agent configuration to specification development.

labs.title: Constructing Executable Specifications
labs.exercise: Construct executable specifications for an authentication module using spec-driven development patterns based on natural language requirements.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, focusing on collaborative workflows between human developers and AI coding agents. Students learn to configure agent skills, tool use, and model context protocols to build reliable software environments. Through practical exercises, students construct executable specifications from natural language requirements and analyze agentic execution loops to debug operational failures. Additionally, they learn to design and assess AI-native software development workflows and evaluation pipelines against specific reliability requirements. The course is taught through three hours of lectures, one tutorial hour, and two practical lab hours per week over thirteen weeks, incorporating hands-on assignments and a collaborative software project. It is not a general introduction to machine learning, a traditional programming course, or a purely theoretical treatment of large language models. Instead, it emphasizes practical, workflow-oriented software engineering practices using emerging developer tools.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The course sequence progresses from foundational setup to advanced workflow evaluation. It begins with configuring agentic protocols (M1), followed by generating executable specifications (M2). Students then analyze and debug execution loops (M3) before designing complete AI-native workflows (M4). This progression builds upon the mandatory prerequisite CSE201, ensuring students possess the necessary object-oriented programming and unit testing foundations to effectively evaluate agent-generated code.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment structure balances practical application and theoretical understanding. Hands-on assignments (25%) and a course project (25%) directly evaluate students' ability to configure protocols (CO1), build specifications (CO2), and design workflows (CO4). Mid-semester (20%) and end-semester (30%) examinations assess their analytical understanding of agentic execution loops, failure debugging (CO3), and workflow justification (CO4), aligning with the practical, workflow-oriented pedagogical emphasis.
narrative.positioning_rationale: This course uniquely focuses on interactive, agent-assisted software development workflows. It differs from CSE701, which applies AI analytically to legacy software engineering artifacts. Unlike CSE581's focus on traditional systems analysis or CSE582's emphasis on legacy maintenance, this course targets greenfield, AI-native development. Finally, while CSE594A is a 2-credit course on broad agentic reasoning, this 4-credit course delivers dedicated, hands-on training in software engineering toolchains and evaluation pipelines.
